Assertions.Description: The configured shortcut pins the ordinary fixture, with actual WS_EX_TOPMOST and visible precedence over an overlapping owned ordinary window.
The pin action displays a composed border around the fixture when highlighting is enabled.
Repeating the configured shortcut removes topmost and restores ordinary overlapping-window precedence.
Unpin removes the fixture's border.
Minimizing the pinned fixture leaves no floating border.
Restoring the minimized fixture retains pinning and restores its surrounding border.
Maximizing the pinned fixture moves the border to its visible frame, not the old bounds; restore normal placement afterward.
After switching to an identity-checked, safely owned temporary desktop, the original fixture's border is absent there.
Returning to the original desktop shows the still-pinned fixture and its surrounding border; remove only the owned temporary desktop.
With no affected user pins, UI disable stops the module and disables dependent activation and appearance controls.
UI re-enable restores controls and module readiness; an ordinary pin/unpin works.
Navigation away and back retains configured values and enablement.
Save a collision-checked temporary pin binding; its key and all modifiers persist and the editor's shortcut/Save/Cancel controls are not clipped.
The saved temporary pin shortcut actually pins and unpins the owned fixture.
The former binding no longer pins the fixture while the temporary binding is saved.
Canceling a different draft preserves the saved binding.
Restoring the original binding restores actual pin/unpin with that binding.
Disabling highlighting removes the border without unpinning the fixture or restarting the module.
Re-enabling highlighting restores the border on the same still-pinned fixture.
Changing custom color from #00CC66 to #FF00FF updates saved values and composed pixels live on the pinned fixture.
Changing thickness from 4 to 18 updates saved values and observed physical border geometry live; record the available monitor/DPI conditions.
Switching from custom to Windows accent mode produces the independently read current accent color.
At frame opacity 100%, straight border interior is solid without mottling or translucent fill; the target interior remains unobscured.
At frame opacity 50%, the border blends with a known opaque backdrop and does not fill the target interior.
On Windows 11, rounded-corners on and off produce their respective surrounding contour while retaining transparent interior.
In a separately authorized clean user/profile without previous module settings, initial UI and saved thickness are 4; never delete this user's configuration to simulate it.
An existing non-default thickness survives ordinary module disable/enable and Settings reopen or navigation, instead of resetting to 4.
Adding only the collision-checked fixture executable to the existing exclusions prevents its pin and border.
After removing the test exclusion and pinning, adding it again immediately removes topmost and border without another shortcut or restart; restore the original list.
With sound enabled and a usable process-attributed audio observer or human listener, successful pin produces feedback; a sound-file open alone is insufficient.
With sound enabled and a usable audio observer/listener, successful unpin produces feedback.
With sound disabled and a usable audio observer/listener, successful pin produces no feedback.
With sound disabled and a usable audio observer/listener, successful unpin produces no feedback.
Given an explicitly authorized elevated owned target, a non-elevated module, enabled sound and a usable observer, an independently established failed state change produces no success sound.
With an owned exclusive D3D fullscreen fixture independently reporting QUNS_RUNNING_D3D_FULL_SCREEN, enabled Game Mode blocking prevents a pin marker.
Under the same independently detected fullscreen condition, disabling Game Mode blocking permits pinning.
After leaving fullscreen, normal pin/unpin works with Game Mode blocking enabled; restore device/window and original setting.
The configured decrease shortcut reduces actual alpha and visible opacity of a pinned layered-alpha-compatible fixture.
Away from maximum opacity, the configured increase shortcut raises actual alpha and visible opacity of the pinned compatible fixture.
Unpinning the originally non-layered fixture restores its original non-layered state after opacity edits.
On a fixture originally layered with known non-default alpha, unpin restores the original alpha and layered flags rather than forcing opaque.
On an unpinned key-observing fixture, both increase and decrease shortcuts leave alpha unchanged and deliver their keys to the application.
Save a distinct collision-checked increase binding with modifiers different from pin; all key/modifier fields persist without changing decrease or pin.
Below maximum alpha, the new increase binding changes opacity and the former binding no longer does so.
Save a distinct collision-checked decrease binding with modifiers different from pin; all key/modifier fields persist without changing increase or pin.
The new decrease binding changes opacity and the former binding no longer does so.
Canceling an opacity-shortcut draft preserves all three saved bindings.
Restore all three original bindings and observe both increase and decrease again on a pinned compatible fixture.
With the option off, the owned classic window's actual system menu has no Always On Top command.
Enabling the option adds exactly one Always On Top command to the owned window's real title-bar system menu.
Reopening that system menu retains exactly one command, without duplication.
Invoking the menu command pins the actual fixture and the reopened menu shows it checked.
Invoking again unpins the fixture and the reopened menu shows it unchecked.
An owned fixture's pre-existing command with the colliding ID retains its original caption and action, without a replacement Always On Top item; restore the option.
With the installed PowerToys extension available, invoking its Always On Top Settings command opens the correct Settings page without pinning another window.
With restorable owned favorites, pin the Settings command and verify it remains available after reopening the palette.
Unpin the command and verify removal from pinned commands while restoring palette and extension lifetime state.
In an already available non-English test locale, the Always On Top command title/subtitle are localized.
Check for updates without install/download preserves recorded non-default Always On Top enablement and runtime state; no channel or automatic-update changes.
In a separately authorized disposable Windows session, a canceled session-end attempt leaves Always On Top usable.
In a separately authorized disposable session, confirmed logoff/shutdown exits the module message loop without a quiesce hang; ordinary disable is not equivalent.

Only with diagnostic consent and an authorized safely restorable restart, enable Diagnostic data/Enable viewing before flows and observe corresponding Always On Top pin/unpin events in the viewer; restore original diagnostic settings.
